guideTitle: The Best Docking Stations for Two Laptops on One Desk
metaTitle: Best KVM Docking Stations for Two Laptops (2026)
metaDescription: We compared KVM docks that share monitors, keyboard and mouse between two laptops on charging per laptop, display output and price, plus single-laptop docks to pair with a separate switch.
introParagraphs: If a work laptop and a personal laptop share one desk, a KVM dock lets both use the same monitors, keyboard and mouse, switching between them without replugging. The key numbers are charging per laptop (60W to 100W here), how many monitors it drives and at what resolution, and whether it accepts USB-C only or also HDMI and DisplayPort inputs.

Four products are all-in-one KVM docks. The other four are standard single-laptop docks, included for a different approach: pairing a full-featured dock with a separate KVM switch, or giving each laptop its own dock. They are marked as such.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $160 to $228 at the time of writing.

av-access-kvm-mst-2-laptops.summary: An AV Access KVM dock with two USB-C MST inputs, dual HDMI 4K and 60W per laptop.
av-access-kvm-mst-2-laptops.description:
This AV Access KVM dock connects two laptops through USB-C MST inputs to dual HDMI 4K monitors, sharing keyboard and mouse, with gigabit Ethernet and EDID emulation to keep displays detected when switching.

Each laptop gets 60W, enough for many ultrabooks but not for higher-power laptops. It costs about $208 at the time of writing, more than the 100W AV Access model.
av-access-kvm-mst-2-laptops.skipIf: Either laptop needs more than 60W; the 100W AV Access suits it.

av-access-kvm-100w-2-laptops.summary: An AV Access KVM dock for two laptops with 100W to each and dual 4K monitors.
av-access-kvm-100w-2-laptops.description:
The 100W AV Access KVM dock is the sensible default: it shares two 4K monitors, keyboard and mouse between two laptops and supplies up to 100W to each, with gigabit Ethernet and EDID emulation.

It costs about $170 at the time of writing, less than the 60W MST model.
pros: Lower price than the MST model
av-access-kvm-100w-2-laptops.skipIf: You need 4K 120Hz; the 13-in-1 KVM lists it.

av-access-8k-kvm-2-computers.summary: An 8K-capable KVM for a laptop and a desktop, with Gigabit Ethernet and hotkey switching.
av-access-8k-kvm-2-computers.description:
This AV Access KVM suits a laptop and a desktop tower sharing one monitor setup, keyboard and mouse, with 8K-capable signal support, Gigabit Ethernet and hotkey switching.

The listing does not state charging wattage for the laptop, and it costs about $213 at the time of writing.
av-access-8k-kvm-2-computers.bestFor: A work laptop and a home desktop.
av-access-8k-kvm-2-computers.skipIf: Both machines are laptops that need charging; the 100W AV Access suits that.

kvm-switch-13in1-aluminum.summary: A 13-in-1 KVM dock with 100W, dual 4K 60Hz or single 4K 120Hz, and HDMI/DP inputs.
kvm-switch-13in1-aluminum.description:
This 13-in-1 KVM dock is the lowest-priced all-in-one option at about $160 at the time of writing, listing 100W, dual 4K 60Hz or single 4K 120Hz output, and USB-C plus HDMI and DisplayPort inputs for mixed machines.

The aluminum case is plug-and-play. The brand is not named in the listing.
kvm-switch-13in1-aluminum.bestFor: Budget two-machine desks, including high-refresh single monitors.
kvm-switch-13in1-aluminum.skipIf: You want an established brand; the AV Access models are branded.

anker-prime-14port-160w.summary: Anker's 14-port, 160W dock, for use with a separate KVM switch.
anker-prime-14port-160w.description:
The Anker Prime is a single-laptop dock, not a KVM: 14 ports, 160W, dual 4K and 10Gbps data. It is included for setups that pair a full-featured dock with a separate KVM switch, or give one laptop its own dock.

It costs about $170 at the time of writing, before the cost of a switch.
cons: Needs a separate switch for two laptops
anker-prime-14port-160w.bestFor: One laptop's permanent dock in a two-laptop setup.
anker-prime-14port-160w.skipIf: You want one box for both laptops; choose a KVM dock.

anker-prime-dl7400-triple-display.summary: Anker's DisplayLink dock for three 4K monitors on one laptop.
anker-prime-dl7400-triple-display.description:
The Anker Prime DL7400 is a single-laptop DisplayLink dock for three 4K 60Hz monitors with 140W output and a cooling fan. It does not switch between laptops.

It suits a desk where the main laptop needs three monitors and a second laptop is connected separately. It costs about $228 at the time of writing.
anker-prime-dl7400-triple-display.bestFor: A primary laptop that needs three screens.
anker-prime-dl7400-triple-display.skipIf: You need switching; choose a KVM dock.

plugable-tb4-dock-m4-m5.summary: Plugable's certified Thunderbolt 4 dock for one Mac or Windows laptop.
plugable-tb4-dock-m4-m5.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is a single-laptop Thunderbolt 4 dock: driverless, 100W charging, dual 4K or single 6K, six USB ports, SD and Ethernet.

In a two-laptop setup it can serve as one machine's dock, typically a MacBook, while the other uses its own. It is not a KVM.
plugable-tb4-dock-m4-m5.bestFor: A Mac in a Mac-plus-Windows desk.
plugable-tb4-dock-m4-m5.skipIf: You want one dock for both laptops.

dell-sd25tb4-pro-smart-dock.summary: Dell's SD25TB4 Thunderbolt 4 smart dock with up to four displays, 130W and 2.5GbE.
dell-sd25tb4-pro-smart-dock.description:
The Dell SD25TB4 is a single-laptop Thunderbolt 4 dock with up to four displays, 130W charging (full rate on Dell laptops), 2.5GbE, Wi-Fi and two Thunderbolt 4 ports.

It suits the Dell work laptop in a two-laptop desk; it is not a KVM.
dell-sd25tb4-pro-smart-dock.bestFor: A Dell work laptop alongside another machine.
dell-sd25tb4-pro-smart-dock.skipIf: You want switching in one box.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A KVM dock shares monitors and peripherals in one box; separate docks plus a switch offer full specs per laptop at higher cost.
60W (AV Access MST) to 100W (AV Access 100W, 13-in-1). Match each laptop's charger.
Dual 4K is typical; the 13-in-1 adds single 4K 120Hz.
USB-C only, or also HDMI/DP for older machines and desktops.

faq.a: A dock that lets two computers share the same monitors, keyboard and mouse, switching between them.
KVM docks here supply 60W or 100W to each laptop. Check against each charger.

faq.q: Can I use two normal docks instead?
faq.a: Yes, with a separate KVM switch or by moving cables; it costs more but gives each laptop a full-featured dock.

bottomLine: For most two-laptop desks, the AV Access 100W KVM dock is the sensible choice, and the 13-in-1 KVM is the budget option with a 4K 120Hz mode. The AV Access 8K suits a laptop-plus-desktop pairing.
The Anker, Plugable and Dell docks are single-laptop docks, worth considering only if you prefer a full dock per machine.
